flags.name: --version
flags.description: show program's version number and exit

flags.name: --help
flags.description: show this help message and exit

flags.name: --port
flags.description: Destination port of the SIP device - eg -p 5060

flags.name: --verbose
flags.description: Increase verbosity

flags.name: --quiet
flags.description: Quiet mode

flags.name: --localport
flags.description: Source port for our packets

flags.name: --externalip
flags.description: IP Address to use as the external ip. Specify this if you have multiple interfaces or if you are behind NAT

flags.name: --bindingip
flags.description: By default we bind to all interfaces. This option overrides that and binds to the specified ip address

flags.name: --timeout
flags.description: This option allows you to trottle the speed at which packets are sent. Change this if you're losing packets. For example try 0.5.

flags.name: --reportback
flags.description: Send the author an exception traceback. Currently sends the command line parameters and the traceback

flags.name: --autogetip
flags.description: Automatically get the current IP address. This is useful when you are not getting any responses back due to SIPVicious not resolving your local IP.

flags.name: --save
flags.description: save the session. Has the benefit of allowing you to resume a previous scan and allows you to export scans

flags.name: --resume
flags.description: resume a previous scan

flags.name: --enablecompact
flags.description: enable compact mode. Makes packets smaller but possibly less compatible

flags.name: --username
flags.description: username to try crack

flags.name: --dictionary
flags.description: specify a dictionary file with passwords or - for stdin

flags.name: --range
flags.description: specify a range of numbers. example: 100-200,300-310,400

flags.name: --extension
flags.description: Extension to crack. Only specify this when the extension is different from the username.

flags.name: --zeropadding
flags.description: the number of zeros used to padd the password. the options "-r 1-9999 -z 4"would give 0001 0002 0003 ... 9999

flags.name: --reusenonce
flags.description: Reuse nonce. Some SIP devices don't mind you reusing the nonce (making them vulnerable to replay attacks). Speeds up the cracking.

flags.name: --template
flags.description: A format string which allows us to specify a template for the extensionsexample svwar.py -e 1-999 --template="123%#04i999" would scan between 1230001999 to 1230999999"

flags.name: --maximumtime
flags.description: Maximum time in seconds to keep sending requests without receiving a response back

flags.name: --enabledefaults
flags.description: Scan for default / typical passwords such as1000,2000,3000 ... 1100, etc. This option is off by default.Use --enabledefaults to enable this functionality

flags.name: --domain
flags.description: force a specific domain name for the SIP message, eg. example.org

flags.name: --requesturi
flags.description: force the first line URI to a specific value; e.g. sip:999@example.org
Scan an IPv6 address

flags.name: --method
flags.description: Specify a SIP method to use
